name: LED matrix module V3
description: 6x6 WS2812D-F8 behind an XL1509-5.0E1 buck, one 100nF per LED. Chained. NOTE: the EasyEDA project is titled 'V2' but is actually V3 - V2 used a different converter and had no decoupling capacitors.

composedOf.note: STOCK 0 at LCSC as of 2026-10-01 - needs an alternative for the next order

3.0 A average forward rectified, 60 V. At 36 V in / 5 V out the duty is 0.14, so it carries 2.16 x 0.86 = 1.86 A average, 62% of rating. Properly specified. Still dissipates ~1 W and is the hottest part, but not the liability first assumed.

busVoltageRange.note: set by the XL1509 input range

fullWhiteCurrent.note: 36 LEDs x 60 mA; EXCEEDS the XL1509's 2.0 A rating by 8%

ratedOutputPower.note: 5 V x 2.0 A, the XL1509's hard cap

busPowerAtFullWhite.note: estimated at ~75% efficiency on a 36 V bus; the datasheet only characterises 12 V in

sustainableBrightness.note: ESTIMATE, thermally limited, not measured. See thermalLimit below.

thermalLimit.summary: Sustained brightness is limited by heat, not by available power. Raising the PD budget cannot raise it.

catchDiodeDissipation.note: 0.5 V Vf x 2.16 A x (1 - 0.139). This is the hottest single part in the module and it has NO protection.

freeAirBudget.note: (125 C TJmax - 25 C ambient) / 100 C/W RthJA

thermalLimit.transientBehaviour: RthJA is a steady-state figure. A SOIC-8 with copper has a thermal time constant of tens of seconds, so sub-second full-white flashes barely move the junction. Only the time-average has to stay under the ceiling.
thermalLimit.verification: UNVERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT. Confirm by running one module at full white on a bench supply and measuring XL1509 case temperature; above ~85 C the junction is near its limit.

icDissipationAt36V.note: modelled at 36 V: VCE 1.2 V x 2.16 A x duty 0.139 (= 5/36) = 0.36 W conduction, plus switching and quiescent. CORRECTED: an earlier note used duty 0.179, which is 5/28 - a 28 V figure under a 36 V label.

failureModes.mechanism: thermal shutdown plus 4 A switch current limit plus frequency foldback
failureModes.note: the IC protects itself, but the thermal shutdown threshold is not specified in the datasheet
~1 W at full white, 62% of its 3 A rating. Adequately specified; unprotected but not the weak point once identified.
saturation and core heating; rating unknown
not at risk from overcurrent; VDD absolute max 5.3 V is the only electrical limit

provenance.composedOf: LEDs and 100nF confirmed from the .epro2 via tools/epro.py; the converter and its parts are from the user's statement, NOT the file
provenance.fullWhiteCurrent: inferred - datasheet C139126 p.3 gives IF = 20 mA/channel as the TEST CONDITION for the LED chip parameters (VF, Iv, lambda-p), not as a specified output drive current. The WS2812D-F8 specifies no drive current anywhere, unlike the SK6812MINI-E which gives IDOUT 10/12/14.5 mA. 20 mA is a sound and conservatively-directed inference, but 14.4 W, 2.16 A, 2.43 A, 4.0 A, every brightness row and the R_SENSE sizing all descend from it
provenance.thermalLimit: modelled from datasheet C61063 p.5 (RthJA) and p.7 (VCE); NOT measured
provenance.inrush: calculated from XL1509 datasheet p.7 bulk cap and bus voltage
provenance.connector: Wago picoMAX series data; selected for the vibration environment
provenance.bulkCapacitorSwap: calculated from XL1509 operating point and cable inductance estimates

maxCableBetweenPoints.note: datasheet C139126 p.1: no extra circuitry needed below 2 m per hop

dataInterface.signalRegeneration: Each pixel reshapes and retransmits, so chain length is not limited by signal degradation - only by the time it takes to clock a frame.
dataInterface.logicLevelWarning: VIH minimum is 0.7 x VDD (datasheet C139126 p.2). On a 5 V module rail that is 3.5 V, and an ESP32-C6 GPIO drives only 3.3 V. THE CONTROLLER CANNOT DRIVE THESE DIRECTLY - a level shifter to 5 V is required on every data line.
dataInterface.datasheetClaimDiscrepancy: Datasheet p.1 claims 'not less than 2048 cascaded points at 30 fps'. That is internally inconsistent: 2048 x 24 bits at 800 kbps is 61 ms, which is 16 fps, not 30. Use the first-principles figure, not the marketing claim.

systemLimits.perceivedBrightnessNote: 'perceived' applies a gamma of 2.2. Luminous output is linear with PWM duty, but human brightness perception is not, so halving the power looks like roughly 73% of the brightness rather than 50%. Degradation with module count is far gentler than the raw power numbers suggest.
systemLimits.mitigation: Parallel data lines fix the refresh limit but NOT the power limit. Splitting the chain across 4 outputs multiplies the achievable frame rate by 4; available watts are unchanged. CORRECTED: the controller uses PARLIO, not RMT. The ESP32-C6 has ONE PARLIO TX unit driving both channels as lanes at data_width=2, and only 2 RMT TX channels - too few for two data channels plus the status chain.
systemLimits.verification: Modelled. The 0.75 efficiency and 0.70 thermal cap are both estimates.

parallelLines.rationale: Frame time is (modules/channels) x 1.08 ms. At 20 modules on 2 channels that is 90 fps, and 180 W caps the wall near 20 modules anyway - channels and power budget run out together. 10 per channel is also the even physical grouping wanted.

frameRateTarget.requirement: ~100 fps preferred for audio-reactive work; 60 fps is the hard floor.
frameRateTarget.note: Includes a 0.28 ms inter-frame latch. 4 channels hold 100 fps to 36 modules while power caps at ~30, so frame rate never becomes the binding constraint anywhere in the operating envelope.
frameRateTarget.nextBottleneck: RETIRED as stated: the README establishes bandwidth is not the limit - 1.56 Mbit/s at the target against 100 Mbit. The real W5500 constraint is BUFFER DEPTH, not throughput: the default 2 kB per-socket RX allocation cannot hold a 20-module frame, which is fixed by setting Sn_RXBUF_SIZE = 8 at init.
frameRateTarget.inherentFlicker: WS2812 internal PWM is ~400 Hz (datasheet C139126 p.1). Independent of frame rate, not changeable from the controller, and the reason these flicker on phone video.

parallelLines.levelShifting: NOT on the controller. The link is a differential pair, so the 3.3 V to 5 V shift for the WS2812s lives on the converter boards, after the receiver.
parallelLines.connectorCurrent: 2.43 A per channel balanced, 28% of the picoMAX's 10 A. The connector is not a binding constraint at 2 channels.

inrush.sourceOfCharge: Each module carries an input bulk capacitor on its CONVERTER board. THE VALUE IS UNREAD: the project library holds 330 uF, 220 uF and 100 uF in 50 V and the placement data does not disambiguate them. Ripple-sizing calculations below use 220 uF; the inrush ramp is deliberately sized for 330 uF as the worst case, so the ambiguity does not affect the design.
inrush.problem: Connecting a 36 V bus to several mF with no limiting draws hundreds of amps for microseconds, limited only by wiring resistance and ESR. The PD source trips and cuts VBUS; connector contacts pit and weld.
inrush.solution: Each channel is switched by its own TPS16630 eFuse (C1849461), which has an integrated 60 V FET. Ramp, current limit, overvoltage cut-off and fast turn-off are in silicon. See the design README's 'Channel switching and inrush' section.

resolution.status: RESOLVED - discrete gate networks abandoned after four failures; replaced by an integrated hot-swap controller.
resolution.history: FOUR attempts, all wrong. The first three were rooted in a gate-to-DRAIN (Miller) capacitor: (1) R_pu 100k/R_pd 1M gave Vgs 3.27 V; (2) 10M/1M/1uF put the ramp on a node with no capacitance, made turn-off 180 s and let the PD step self-turn-on the FET; (3) dropping the master FET moved the same faults onto channel switches with 27x more load capacitance - 8.2 A during the PD step against a 5 A contract. The fourth moved to a gate-to-SOURCE capacitor with a diode bypassing the pull-up, and was written up as settled before review found two independent fatal errors: a diode across a gate-source pull-up cannot discriminate direction, because the resistor carries current the same way when turning off and when the pull-down drags the gate low, so it clamps Vgs and the FET never enhances; and a gate-to-source capacitor cannot set a ramp in a common-source switch, because the drain transition happens inside the Miller plateau where Vgs is constant and C_gs therefore carries no current at all.
resolution.whyIntegrated: A discrete network has to deliver ramp, current limit, turn-off and dV/dt immunity from one capacitor and two resistors, and those requirements pull against each other. No value set reconciles them.
resolution.designPoint: Per channel: TPS16630 eFuse with R_ILIM 3.24 kOhm (5.56 A), C_dVdT 220 nF (Eq. 2 gives a 165 ms ramp, Eq. 1 gives 0.72 A constant inrush), UVLO/OVP string 723k/249k/29.4k (UVLO 4.32 V, OVP 40.9 V). Ramp time has no C_OUT term, so there is no module-count ceiling from start-up.
resolution.sideEffects: The integrated FET removed the discrete switch and the sense resistor, and takes the channel path from 60 V (1.03x the TVS clamp) to 67 V absolute (1.15x). Its OVP reference is +/-2% against the LM5069 comparator's +/-10%, which is what lets a 40.9 V trip fit between the 37.8 V maximum bus and the modules' 45 V absolute - a window the previous part could not fit into.
resolution.soa: Not a calculation any more. The TPS16630 regulates its own junction temperature through start-up and TI publishes it powering into 15 mF against 3.3 mF per channel here. The discrete P-FET SOA question that cost four review rounds does not arise.
resolution.contractHeadroom: Both channels can be released together: 0.72 A each, 1.44 A against a 5.0 A contract.
resolution.cost: Dissipation: 31 mOhm integrated against 9.5 mOhm discrete plus a 10 mOhm shunt, so 0.53 W for the pair against 0.28 W. Thermal headroom 1.29x -> 1.20x. Turn-on delay is 11.6 ms, replacing the LM5069's multi-second insertion timer.

storedEnergyAt36V._note: CORRECTED: these were computed at 28 V with 220 uF/module while the key says 36 V. Recomputed as 0.5 * N * 330 uF * 36^2, the capacitance the design sizes the ramp for.

inrush.slewRequired_note: CORRECTED: these were computed at 28 V with 220 uF/module while labelled 36 V. Recomputed at 36 V with the 330 uF the design sizes for.
inrush.storedEnergyAt36V_note: CORRECTED: these were computed at 28 V with 220 uF/module while labelled 36 V. Recomputed at 36 V with the 330 uF the design sizes for.

connector.whyThisOne: Push-in spring termination holds constant force, unlike a screw that backs out under vibration. Male headers carry an integrated locking latch, so the plug cannot walk out. Both vibration failure modes covered without a crimp tool.
connector.sourcing: Reichelt or Mouser, NOT LCSC - so JLCPCB cannot place it and the two controller-side headers are hand-soldered. Acceptable for two parts.
connector.supersedes: Wurth WR-PHD 2.54 mm (3 A, no keying, no latch) and the Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 / KF2EDG alternatives considered. Micro-Fit was equally vibration-sound (crimp + latch) but needs a 50-150 EUR crimp tool and is not field-repairable with a screwdriver.
connector.consequenceForLimits: At 10 A the connector stops being a binding constraint: the 2.43 A balanced case is 24%, the 2.80 A worst case 28%, and a 4.0 A full-white flash 40%. The 3 A limit stack that drove the per-channel software cap and the PPTC no longer applies. The binding limit moves to the CABLE - 0.5 mm2 is roughly 5 A chassis wiring, ~2.5 A bundled (IEC 60228).
connector.openPoint: RESOLVED: Reichelt WAGO 2091-1424 (picoMAX 3.5 angled pin header, 4-pole, art. 136753, EUR 0.77) on the board, WAGO 2091-1104 (spring plug, art. 136715) on the cable. Straight-pin alternative 2091-1524 (art. 136759, EUR 3.10). A 20-module run needs 20 plugs - easy to forget when ordering.

orientationHandling.detail: picoMAX is polarised so the plug cannot go in backwards or offset by a pole. Each module also sits in a hard shell with all LEDs facing the same way, so physical arrangement enforces orientation before the connector matters.
orientationHandling.residualRisk: A mis-wired cable at assembly, not a mis-plugged one. A/B swapped is non-destructive (inverted data, chain does not light); power onto a data pole destroys the transceiver. Worth a continuity check on the first cable of a batch.

connector.pinoutRationale: The differential pair takes two poles, power and ground the other two - exactly 4, which is why the 4-pole part works without going to 5.

cabling.topology: controller -> ONE long cable -> first converter board; modules then chain board-to-board like a snake, adjacent on the wall. Only the first cable has length.
cabling.bindingLimit: power, not data - the differential pair removed the data limit

recommendedGauge.note: a differential pair at 800 kbps is good for tens of metres, so the 5% voltage-drop line is now the only constraint

signalIntegrity: twist A and B together as a pair
120 ohm termination at the far end, on the first converter board
keep the pair away from the +36 V conductor and its converter switching noise

environment.context: Mounted on a soundwall for tekno. Sustained high-amplitude vibration.
environment.consequence: Gates part selection. Screw terminations and mass-on-long-leads parts are both disfavoured.
affectedParts: module bulk electrolytic (radial, mass on two leads) - the classic vibration solder-joint fatigue case; bond the body or move to SMD polymer / MLCC bank
JK60-300 PPTC (10.2 mm radial THT) - same geometry, lighter
converter board inductors - heavy and tall
mechanical: standoffs at several points, not two corners - an unsupported span resonates and amplifies acceleration at mid-board parts
cable strain relief near each connector so cable movement does not load contacts

bulkCapacitorSwap.status: PARKED - module-side change, not blocking the controller
bulkCapacitorSwap.motivation: Electrolytics are bulky, wear out as the electrolyte dries, and are mass on long leads in a vibration environment. The user wants them gone.
bulkCapacitorSwap.finding1_ripple: The input cap only needs ~8 uF for ripple. At 36 V in / 5 V out / 2 A the duty is 0.139 and input RMS ripple current is 0.69 A at 150 kHz; 8 uF holds input ripple to 0.2 V. The existing 220-330 uF is roughly 40x oversized for this.
bulkCapacitorSwap.finding2_damping: Damping is what the big cap is really doing, and it is the reason a straight swap to ceramic is unsafe. Cable inductance plus input capacitance forms a resonant tank: ~2 uH (2 m) with 20 uF rings at 25 kHz needing 0.32 ohm; 5 uH (5 m) at 15.9 kHz needing 0.50 ohm; 10 uH (10 m) at 11.3 kHz needing 0.71 ohm. A wet electrolytic's ESR supplies that naturally. LED flashes are exactly the load steps that excite a 15 kHz resonance.
bulkCapacitorSwap.finding3_inrush: Shrinking the cap collapses the inrush problem: 10 modules x 330 uF = 3300 uF needing a 59 ms ramp, versus 10 x 20 uF = 200 uF needing 4 ms.
bulkCapacitorSwap.directionIfPursued: Ceramic bank for ripple and HF, plus a deliberate damping element - either an SMD polymer/hybrid (long life, low profile, no long leads) or an explicit RC damping branch sized per Middlebrook (Cdamp ~4x Cin, R ~ sqrt(L/C)). Note only the FIRST module in each chain sees the long cable; downstream links are board-to-board with little inductance, so they could be all-ceramic.
bulkCapacitorSwap.caveat: At a 36 V bus every candidate needs a >=50 V rating, which thins the polymer options considerably.
